dedupe_keys.name: grid interactive efficient building technology cost performance and lifetime characteristics

description: This dataset holds the raw data behind the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report on the cost, performance and lifetime of grid-interactive efficient building (GEB) technologies. It was published on Zenodo on 7 January 2021 by Valerie Nubbe, Kyung Lee, Alejandro Valdez and Ed Barbour of Guidehouse, which collected the data, and Jared Langevin of LBNL. It characterises residential and commercial building technologies and equipment that can provide grid services, chosen from the US Department of Energy GEB technical report series, ENERGY STAR connected certified products and input from national laboratory researchers. Each technology has a typical case and a connected or grid-interactive case, with current DOE appliance standard levels where available; values are for 2020 with projections for 2030, 2040 and 2050. Coverage: United States technology markets. Access: one Excel workbook on Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: enabling technologies such as smart meters and energy management software, and non-building technologies such as EV chargers and PV inverters, are out of scope; definitions vary by technology. Simulation uses: demand flexibility and technology adoption inputs to building stock and energy system models. Related records: Scout benchmark scenarios and the EIA RECS and CBECS surveys.
name: Grid-Interactive Efficient Building technology cost, performance and lifetime characteristics
